prompt:
I want to get rid of docs/stock-feed.md. Can you move what belongs next to the code into comments, and remove the page if nothing on it needs to stay a document?

Input files: README.md, docs/marketplace.md, docs/stock-feed.md, stock/__init__.py, stock/feed.py, stock/format.py, stock/rows.py, tests/__init__.py, tests/test_feed.py
assertions: stock_rows gains no comment or docstring line about write_feed, the merge pass or why its rows must be sorted, negated or not; and no other added comment, docstring or document line says that stock_rows() must return sorted rows, that write_feed() needs its rows in SKU order, or that a row out of order is skipped.
The MKT-204 reason for the quantity cap is in a code comment or docstring and in no document.
The quantity-cap reason sits at MAX_FEED_QTY or feed_line in stock/format.py (placement, heuristic).
stock_rows gains no comment or docstring lines, and no added comment or docstring repeats the page's restatements (SKUs with no stock are left out; lines are tab-separated).
No code changed: every Python file's code is the same apart from comments and docstrings, and the hidden behaviour tests pass (write_feed sorts its own input, so rows in any order are all written).
Every original comment and docstring is kept word for word, and README.md and docs/marketplace.md lose nothing.
No file was added to the repository.
The reply tells the user, in one bullet or paragraph, that the page's claim that stock_rows() must sort for write_feed is out of date, because write_feed sorts the rows itself.
The reply gives a fate for each claim on the page: the no-stock filter, the sort, the tab-separated line and the MKT-204 cap.
